findings.title: All success criteria trace to tasks; no scope creep
findings.description:
Cross-referencing the LLD's Success Criteria against the tasks:

- **Functional 1** (slice-branch body cites design, checked/unchecked items, review provenance) → Tasks 7, 8, 9, 11 (11.2's "full inputs" case asserts the deterministic facts verbatim).
- **Functional 2** (unplanned repository: five sections, three no-input lines, creation succeeds) → 11.2's unplanned-repository case plus 16.2's walkthrough step 4.
- **Functional 3** (merged ancestor's review excluded) → 8.2's explicitly load-bearing in-range-vs-ancestor case.
- **Functional 4–5** (integration-branch refusal naming the branch / integration-branch base with printed source) → 5.1's D1 table and 5.2's per-row cases, including "the refusal case asserts the branch name appears in the message and that `default_branch` was never called"; printing is in 13.1.
- **Functional 6** (unpushed/behind failures name the push command before any write) → Task 6, with the before-write ordering asserted in 13.2 ("a precondition failure means the composer was never called").
- **Functional 7** (missing section fails the presence check with zero write calls) → 12.2 and 13.2 ("a failed presence check exits 1 with no write").
- **Functional 8** (title: deterministic on a slice branch with no model call; `--title` overrides; empty/over-72 falls back to the first commit subject) → Task 10a and 10a.2's eight cases, including the "composer is never called" assertion.
- **Functional 9** (dry-run/real equality) → 13.2's equality case plus 13.1's single-binding requirement (D8).
- **Functional 10** (identity refusal exits non-zero naming the reason, no write) → 13.2's identity-refusal case; the reason rendering via `render_code_host_error` is pinned in 14.1.
- **Functional 11** (one recorded live creation) → 16.2 step 5, with the URL recorded as evidence.
- **Technical 1** (timeout constants at all five call sites) → 14.1, including the `GIT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` vs `HOST_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` assertion from design review F007.
- **Technical 2** (provider failure: exit non-zero, ERROR log, nothing created) → 10.1's process-boundary handler and 10.2's assertion (F008).
- **Technical 3** (default path makes exactly one write, after every read) → 13.2's happy-path and ordering assertions.
- **Technical 4** (`review/` does not import `pr/`) → 15.1.
- **Technical 5** (checkbox parser with real-task-file fixture) → 2.1/2.2, including the "this file once it exists" fixture named in the criterion.
- **Technical 6** (pyright/ruff clean) → 16.1.
- **Technical 7** (`summary_oneshot` docstring correction with a routing test) → 15.2.
- The Verification Walkthrough's six steps → 16.2 verbatim, with the walkthrough rewrite in 16.3.

Every task traces back to a criterion or a design decision (D1–D8, D4a); nothing is scope creep. Task 15's two corrections are both owed items named in the design and repeated in the technical criteria. The test tasks are exactly those the criteria demand — no extra test surface. No NFR is restated in the slice, so no `tests/load/` task is required.

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with pattern are sound
findings.description: Dependencies are respected end to end: the two pure parsers (Tasks 1–2) land first and alone; git helpers (Task 3) and the `resolve_locator` extraction (Task 4) precede their consumers; refusal paths (5, 6) precede gathering (7, 8), which precede assembly (9), composition (10, 10a, 11), the check (12), and the wiring (13). This matches the LLD's "Implementation Notes → Order" and the D8 constraint that every model-free refusal precedes the model call. Each implementation task is immediately followed by its test task (1→2, 3→3.2, 4→4.2, 5→5.2, 6→6.2, 7→7.2, 8→8.2, 9→9.2, 10→10.2, 10a→10a.2, 11→11.2, 12→12.2, 13→13.2). Task 14 is a test-only task but correctly placed after 13 — the failure matrix cannot run before the command exists. No circular dependencies.

findings.title: Local head sha for the pushed-branch precondition is unnamed
findings.description: `check_head_pushed` takes `local_sha: str` as an input, but no task says how the command obtains the local head sha. Task 3 adds only `current_branch` (a branch *name*) and `commits_in_range` (which needs a base — and per Task 13.1's ordering, base selection runs *after* the precondition). The wiring step in Task 13 therefore depends on an acquisition (`git rev-parse HEAD`) that exists in no task's steps. This is completable — the parameter name makes the requirement clear and the acquisition is idiomatic — but naming it in Task 3's helpers or Task 13.1's steps would remove the last unspecified input on the path.

findings.title: "No host call is made" in 12.2 conflates reads with writes
findings.description: Task 12.2 asserts "the failure path creates nothing — no host call is made", while the success criterion says "verified by the fake runner recording zero write calls". At command level the check runs *after* several legitimate host reads (`identify_operator`, `branch_exists`, possibly `default_branch`), so "no host call" would be literally wrong there; 13.2 (line 309) phrases it correctly as "no write". In the unit-level `tests/pr/test_body.py` context the assertion is trivially true. Reconciling the phrasing to "no write" would keep the two levels consistent.
